41 Rose::Cmdline::
42 makeSysIncludeList(const Rose_STL_Container<string>& dirs, Rose_STL_Container<string>& result, bool using_nostdinc_option)
43  {
44 #ifdef _MSC_VER
45  string includeBase = findRoseSupportPathFromBuild("include-staging", "include\\edg");
46  // NP (3/18/2020) Need to switch the slash direction
47  for(int i = 0; i < includeBase.length(); ++i) if(includeBase[i] == '/') includeBase[i] = '\\';
48 #else
49  string includeBase = findRoseSupportPathFromBuild("include-staging", "include/edg");
50 #endif
51  for (Rose_STL_Container<string>::const_iterator i = dirs.begin(); i != dirs.end(); ++i)
52  {
53  ROSE_ASSERT (!i->empty());
54 #ifdef _MSC_VER
55  string fullPath = (*i)[1] == ':' ? *i : (includeBase + "\\" + *i);
56 #else
57  string fullPath = (*i)[0] == '/' ? *i : (includeBase + "/" + *i);
58 #endif
59 
60  // DQ (11/8/2011): We want to exclude the /usr/include directory since it will be search automatically by EDG.
61  // If we include it here it will become part of the -sys_include directories and that will cause it to
62  // be searched before the -I<directory> options (which is incorrect).
63  if ( SgProject::get_verbose() > 1 )
64  {
65  printf ("In makeSysIncludeList(): Building commandline: --sys_include %s fullPath = %s \n",(*i).c_str(),fullPath.c_str());
66  }
67 
68  if (*i == "/usr/include")
69  {
70  if ( SgProject::get_verbose() > 1 )
71  {
72  printf ("Filtering out from the sys_include paths: *i = %s \n",(*i).c_str());
73  }
74  }
75  else
76  {
77  // DQ (2/1/2015): Adding support for optional use of gnu nostdinc option. This causes system
78  // directories to not be searched, however, we still need to reference at least one ROSE
79  // specific directory. This is required for compiling some kernel level applications.
80 
81  // result.push_back("--sys_include");
82  // result.push_back(fullPath);
83  if (using_nostdinc_option == true)
84  {
85  // Pei-Hung (03/01/2021): using only gcc_HEADERS and g++_HEADERS to check the header file directories is not sufficient.
86  // The directory names change according the the executable names of gcc and g++.
87 
88  const char* CC_Basename = BACKEND_C_COMPILER_NAME_WITHOUT_PATH;
89  const char* CXX_Basename = BACKEND_CXX_COMPILER_NAME_WITHOUT_PATH;
90  string CC_Headername(CC_Basename);
91  string CXX_Headername(CXX_Basename);
92  CC_Headername += "_HEADERS";
93  CXX_Headername += "_HEADERS";
94  if (*i == CC_Headername || *i == CXX_Headername)
95  {
96  result.push_back("--sys_include");
97  result.push_back(fullPath);
98  }
99  }
100  else
101  {
102  result.push_back("--sys_include");
103  result.push_back(fullPath);
104  }
105  }
106  }
107  }

150 // DQ (1/16/2008): This function was moved from the commandling_processing.C file to support the debugging specific to binary analysis
151 /* This function not only looks at the file name, but also checks that the file exists, can be opened for reading, and has
152  * specific values for its first two bytes. Checking the first two bytes here means that each time we add support for a new
153  * magic number in the binary parsers we have to remember to update this list also. Another problem is that the binary
154  * parsers understand a variety of methods for neutering malicious binaries -- transforming them in ways that make them
155  * unrecognized by the operating system on which they're intended to run (and thus unrecongizable also by this function).
156  * Furthermore, CommandlineProcessing::isBinaryExecutableFile() contains similar magic number checking. [RPM 2010-01-15] */
157 bool
158 CommandlineProcessing::isExecutableFilename(string name)
159  {
160  initExecutableFileSuffixList();
161 
162  if (SgProject::get_verbose() > 0)
163  {
164  printf ("CommandlineProcessing::isExecutableFilename(): name = %s validExecutableFileSuffixes.size() = %" PRIuPTR " \n",name.c_str(),validExecutableFileSuffixes.size());
165  }
166 
167  int length = name.size();
168  for (string &suffix : validExecutableFileSuffixes)
169  {
170  int jlength = suffix.size();
171 
172  if ( (length > jlength) && (name.compare(length - jlength, jlength, suffix) == 0) )
173  {
174  // Open file for reading
175  if (isValidFileWithExecutableFileSuffix(name))
176  {
177  FILE* f = fopen(name.c_str(), "rb");
178  ASSERT_not_null(f);
179 
180  // Check if this is a binary executable file!
181  int char0 = fgetc(f);
182  int char1 = fgetc(f);
183  fclose(f);
184 
185  // Note that there may be more executable formats that this simple test will not catch.
186  // The first character of an ELF binary is '\177' and for a PE binary it is 'M'
187  bool isExe = (char0 == 0x7F && char1 == 0x45) || (char0 == 0x4D && char1 == 0x5A);
188  if (isExe) {
189  return true;
190  }
191  }
192  }
193  }
194 
195  return false;
196  }

219  return true;
220  }
221  }
222  }
223 
224  return false;

410 // Build the list of isolated file names from the command line
411 Rose_STL_Container<string>
412 CommandlineProcessing::generateSourceFilenames(Rose_STL_Container<string> argList, bool binaryMode)
413  {
414  Rose_STL_Container<string> sourceFileList;
415 
416 #ifdef ROSE_BUILD_JAVA_LANGUAGE_SUPPORT
417  // DQ (1/10/2019): This is an issue when using ROSE for non Java language support in some environment.
418  // This was the cause of a bug that contaminated the backend compiler command line for an installation
419  // or ROSE for a specific sponsor.
420 
421  // Expand Javac's @argfile since it may contain filenames
422  argList = Rose::Cmdline::Java::ExpandArglist(argList);
423 #endif
424 
425  // Find out if the command line is a source code compile line
426  bool isSourceCodeCompiler = false;
427 
428  // skip the 0th entry since this is just the name of the program
429  Rose_STL_Container<string>::iterator j = argList.begin();
430  ASSERT_require(argList.size() > 0);
431  j++;
432 
433  while (j != argList.end())
434  {
435  string &arg = *j;
436  if (arg.size() == 2 && arg[0] == '-' && arg[1] == 'o')
437  {
438  isSourceCodeCompiler = true;
439  break;
440  }
441  j++;
442  }
443 
444  // skip the 0th entry since this is just the name of the program
445  Rose_STL_Container<string>::iterator i = argList.begin();
446  ASSERT_require(argList.size() > 0);
447  i++;
448 
449  while (i != argList.end())
450  {
451  // Count up the number of filenames (if it is ZERO then this is likely a
452  // link line called using the compiler (required for template processing
453  // in C++ with most compilers)) if there is at least ONE then this is the
454  // source file. Currently their can be up to maxFileNames = 256 files
455  // specified.
456 
457  // most options appear as -<option>
458  // have to process +w2 (warnings option) on some compilers so include +<option>
459 
460  const string &arg = *i;
461 
462  // Ignore things that would be obvious options using a "-" or "+" prefix.
463  if ( arg.empty() || ((arg[0] != '-') && (arg[0] != '+')) )
464  {
465  if (!isSourceFilename(arg) &&
466  (binaryMode || !isObjectFilename(arg)) &&
467  (binaryMode || isExecutableFilename(arg)))
468  {
469  if (isSourceCodeCompiler == false || binaryMode == true) {
470  sourceFileList.push_back(arg);
471  }
472  goto incrementPosition;
473  }
474 
475  // Add source files based on file suffix
476  if (!isObjectFilename(arg) && isSourceFilename(arg))
477  {
478  sourceFileList.push_back(arg);
479  goto incrementPosition;
480  }
481  }
482 
483  // Look for rose options that take filenames that would accidentally be considered as source files.
484  if (isOptionTakingSecondParameter(arg))
485  {
486  if (isOptionTakingThirdParameter(arg))
487  {
488  // Jump over the next argument when such options are identified.
489  i++;
490  }
491  // Jump over the next argument when such options are identified.
492  i++;
493  }
494 
495 incrementPosition:
496 
497  i++;
498  }
499 
500  if (SgProject::get_verbose() > 1)
501  {
502  printf ("sourceFileList = %s \n",StringUtility::listToString(sourceFileList).c_str());
503  printf ("######################### Leaving of CommandlineProcessing::generateSourceFilenames() ############################ \n");
504  }
505 
506  return sourceFileList;
507  }

509 static std::string const & __str_id(std::string const & str) { return str; }
510 
511 template <typename T, typename F=decltype(__str_id)>
512 static void split_string(std::string const & str, T & res, char sep = ',', F & f = __str_id) {
513  size_t pos = 0;
514  size_t prev = 0;
515  while (pos < str.size()) {
516  if (str[pos] == sep) {
517  res.push_back(f(str.substr(prev, pos-prev)));
518  pos++;
519  prev = pos;
520  } else {
521  pos++;
522  }
523  }
524  res.push_back(f(str.substr(prev, pos-prev)));
525 }

530 void
531 SgProject::processCommandLine(const vector<string>& input_argv)
532  {
533  // This functions only copies the command line and extracts information from the
534  // command line which is useful at the SgProject level (other information useful
535  // at the SgFile level is not extracted).
536  // Specifically:
537  // 1) --help is processed (along with -help, to be friendly)
538  // 2) -o <filename> is processed (since both the compilation and the linking
539  // phases must know the output file name and it makes sense to process that once).
540  // 3) Lists of files and libraries are processed (sense they too are required in
541  // both compilation and linking). (e.g. -l<libname>, -L <directory>, <libname>.a,
542  // <filename>.C, <filename>.c, -I<directory name>, <filename>.h
543  // NOTE: there is no side-effect to argc and argv. Thus the original ROSE translator can
544  // see all options. Any ROSE or EDG specific options can be striped by calling the
545  // appropriate functions to strip them out.
546 
547  // This function now makes an internal copy of the command line parameters to
548  // allow the originals to remain unmodified (SLA modifies the command line).
549 
550  // local copies of argc and argv variables
551  // The purpose of building local copies is to avoid
552  // the modification of the command line by SLA (to save the original command line)
553  vector<string> local_commandLineArgumentList = input_argv;
554  { // Perform normalization on CLI before processing and storing
555 
556  // Turn "-I <path>" into "-I<path>" for subsequent processing
557  local_commandLineArgumentList =
558  Rose::Cmdline::NormalizeIncludePathOptions(
559  local_commandLineArgumentList);
560  }
561 
562 #ifdef ROSE_BUILD_JAVA_LANGUAGE_SUPPORT
563  // DQ (1/10/2019): This is an issue when using ROSE for non Java language support in some environment.
564  // This was the cause of a bug that contaminated the backend compiler command line for an installation
565  // or ROSE for a specific sponsor.
566 
567  { // Expand Javac's @argfile before CLI processing
568  local_commandLineArgumentList =
569  Rose::Cmdline::Java::ExpandArglist(
570  local_commandLineArgumentList);
571  }
572 #endif
573 
574 // DQ (11/29/2020): Clang linker does not understand the -pthread option (issues a warning, but I think it is a makefile commandline issue).
575 // Add "-D_REENTRANT" if "-pthread" is present before we save the command-line or do any other processing.
576  vector<string>::iterator pthread =
577  find(local_commandLineArgumentList.begin(), local_commandLineArgumentList.end(), "-pthread");
578  if (pthread != local_commandLineArgumentList.end())
579  local_commandLineArgumentList.insert(++pthread, "-D_REENTRANT");
580 
581  // Save a deep copy fo the original command line input the the translator
582  // pass in out copies of the argc and argv to make clear that we don't modify argc and argv
583  set_originalCommandLineArgumentList( local_commandLineArgumentList );
584 
585  ASSERT_not_null(p_fileList_ptr);
586  p_fileList_ptr->get_listOfFiles().clear();
587 
588  // return value for calls to SLA
589  int optionCount = 0;
590 
591  //
592  // help option (allows alternative --h or --help)
593  //
594  // Use 1 at end of argument list to SLA to force removal of option from argv and decrement of agrc
595  // optionCount = sla(&argc, argv, "--", "($)", "(h|help)",1);
596  optionCount = sla_none(local_commandLineArgumentList, "--", "($)", "(h|help)",1);
597  if( optionCount > 0 )
598  {
599  // Rose::usage(0);
600  cout << version_message() << endl;
601  SgFile::usage(0);
602  exit(0);
603  }
604 
605  //
606  // version option (allows alternative --version or --V)
607  //

1058  // DQ (10/16/2005):
1059  // Build versions of argc and argv that are separate from the input_argc and input_argv
1060  // (so that we can be clear that there are no side-effects to the original argc and argv
1061  // that come from the user's ROSE translator. Mostly we want to use the short names
1062  // (e.g. "argc" and "argv").
1063  vector<string> argv = get_originalCommandLineArgumentList();
1064  ROSE_ASSERT(argv.size() > 0);
1065 
1066  // Note that we need to process this option before the interpretation of the filenames (below).
1067  if ( CommandlineProcessing::isOption(argv,"-rose:","(binary|binary_only)",true) == true )
1068  {
1069  if ( SgProject::get_verbose() >= 1 )
1070  printf ("Binary mode ON \n");
1071  set_binary_only(true);
1072  }
1073 
1074  // The specification of "-rose:binary" causes filenames to be interpreted
1075  // differently if they are object files or libary archive files.
1076  p_sourceFileNameList = CommandlineProcessing::generateSourceFilenames(argv,get_binary_only());
1077 
1078  // Build a list of source, object, and library files on the command line
1079  for (unsigned int i = 1; i < argv.size(); i++)
1080  {
1081  // find the source code filenames and modify them to be the output filenames
1082  unsigned int length = argv[i].size();
1083 
1084  // DQ (2/4/2009): Only put *.o files into the objectFileNameList is they are not being
1085  // processed as binary source files (targets for analysis, as opposed to linking).
1086  if ( (get_binary_only() == false) && (CommandlineProcessing::isObjectFilename(argv[i]) == true) )
1087  {
1088  p_objectFileNameList.push_back(argv[i]);
1089  }
1090 
1091  // look only for .a files (library files)
1092  if ( (length > 2) &&
1093  ( (argv[i][0] != '-') && (argv[i][0] != '+') ) &&
1094  ( (argv[i][length-2] == '.') && (argv[i][length-1] == 'a') ) )
1095  {
1096  std::string libraryFile = argv[i];
1097  p_libraryFileList.push_back(libraryFile);
1098 
1099  // DQ (2/4/2009): Make sure that this is not handled incorrectly is we wanted it to be a target for binary analysis.
1100  // If so, then is should end up on the source code list (target list for analysis).
1101  if (get_binary_only() == true)
1102  {
1103  printf ("This may be an error, since the library archive should be treated as a source file for binary analysis. \n");
1104  }
1105  }
1106

1110  {

1112  {
1113  std::cout << "[INFO] [Cmdline] "
1114  << "Processing -dylib_file"

1116  }
1117 
1118  if (argv.size() == (i+1))
1119  {
1120  throw std::runtime_error("Missing required argument to -dylib_file");
1121  }
1122  else
1123  {
1124  // TODO: Save library argument; for now just skip over the argument
1125  ++i;
1126  if (SgProject::get_verbose() > 1)
1127  {
1128  std::cout << "[INFO] [Cmdline] "
1129  << "Processing -dylib_file: argument="
1130  << "'" << argv[i] << "'"
1131  << std::endl;

1407 //------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1408 // Cmdline
1409 //------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1410 std::vector<std::string>
1411 Rose::Cmdline::
1412 NormalizeIncludePathOptions (std::vector<std::string> &argv)
1413 {
1414  std::vector<std::string> r_argv;
1415 
1416  bool looking_for_include_path_arg = false;
1417  for (string &arg : argv)
1418  {
1419  // Must be first since there could be, for example, "-I -I",
1420  // in which case, the else if branch checking for -I would
1421  // be entered.
1422  if (looking_for_include_path_arg)
1423  {
1424  looking_for_include_path_arg = false; // reset for next iteration
1425 
1426  // Sanity check
1427  bool is_directory = boost::filesystem::is_directory(arg);
1428  if (false == is_directory)
1429  {
1430  // DQ (3/15/2017): Fixed to use mlog message logging.
1431  if (Rose::ir_node_mlog[Rose::Diagnostics::DEBUG])
1432  {
1433  std::cout << "[WARN] "
1434  << "Invalid argument to -I; path does not exist: "
1435  << "'" << arg << "'"
1436  << std::endl;
1437  }
1438  }
1439 #ifdef _MSC_VER
1440  // ensure that the path is quoted on Windows.
1441  r_argv.push_back("-I\"" + arg + "\"");
1442 #else
1443  r_argv.push_back("-I" + arg + "");
1444 #endif
1445  }
1446  else if ((arg.size() >= 2) && (arg[0] == '-') && (arg[1] == 'I'))
1447  {
1448  // -I <path>: There is a space between the option and the argument...
1449  // ^
1450  //
1451  // ...meaning this current argument is exactly "-I".
1452  //
1453  if (arg.size() == 2)
1454  {
1455  looking_for_include_path_arg = true;
1456  continue; // next iteration should be the path argument
1457  }
1458  else
1459  {
1460  // no normalization required for -I<path>, but ensure
1461  // that the path is quoted on Windows.
1462 #ifdef _MSC_VER
1463  if (arg[2] != '"')
1464  {
1465  arg.insert(2, "\"");
1466  arg.append("\"");
1467  }
1468 #endif
1469  r_argv.push_back(arg);
1470  }
1471  }
1472  else // not an include path option
1473  {
1474  r_argv.push_back(arg);
1475  }
1476  }//argv.each
1477 
1478  // Found -I option but no accompanying <path> argument
1479  if (looking_for_include_path_arg == true)
1480  {
1481  std::cout << "[FATAL] "
1482  << "Missing required argument to -I; expecting '-I<path>'"
1483  << std::endl;
1484  exit(1);
1485  }
1486  else
1487  {
1488  return r_argv;
1489  }
1490 }//NormalizeIncludePathOptions (std::vector<std::string>& argv)

1932 void
1933 Rose::Cmdline::Ada::
1934 StripRoseOptions (std::vector<std::string>& argv)
1935 {
1936  auto isAdaOption = [stripArg = 0](const std::string& arg) mutable -> bool
1937  {
1938  if (stripArg > 0)
1939  {
1940  --stripArg;
1941  return true;
1942  }
1943 
1944  if (Rose::Cmdline::Ada::OptionRequiresArgument(arg))
1945  {
1946  stripArg = 1;
1947  return true;
1948  }
1949 
1950  return arg.rfind(ADA_OPTION_PREFIX, 0) == 0;
1951  };
1952 
1953  std::vector<std::string>::iterator zz = argv.end();
1954  std::vector<std::string>::iterator pos = std::remove_if(argv.begin(), zz, isAdaOption);
1955  argv.erase(pos, zz);
1956 }

1962 bool
1963 Rose::Cmdline::Java::
1964 OptionRequiresArgument (const std::string& option)
1965 {
1966  return
1967  // Javac Options
1968  option == "-bootclasspath" ||

1971  option == "-sourcepath" ||
1972  option == "-d" ||
1973  option == "-source" ||
1974  option == "-target" ||
1975  option == "-encoding" ||
1976  option == "-s" ||
1977  // ROSE Options
1978  option == "-rose:java:cp" ||
1979  option == "-rose:java:classpath" ||
1980  option == "-rose:java:sourcepath" ||
1981  option == "-rose:java:d" ||
1982  option == "-rose:java:ds" ||
1983  option == "-rose:java:source" ||
1984  option == "-rose:java:target" ||
1985  option == "-rose:java:encoding" ||
1986  option == "-rose:java:ecj:jvm_options";
1987 }// Cmdline:Java:::OptionRequiresArgument
1988 
1989 void
1990 Rose::Cmdline::Java::
1991 StripRoseOptions (std::vector<std::string>& argv)
1992 {
1993  std::string argument;
1994 
1995  // (1) Options WITHOUT an argument
1996  sla(argv, "-rose:", "($)", "(j|J|java|Java)",1);
1997 
1998  //
1999  // (2) Options WITH an argument
2000  //
2001 
2002  Cmdline::Java::Ecj::StripRoseOptions(argv);
2003 
2004  // Remove Java options with ROSE-Java prefix; option arguments removed
2005  // by generateOptionWithNameParameterList.
2006  //
2007  // For example,
2008  //
2009  // BEFORE: argv = [-rose:java:classpath, "/some/class/path", -rose:verbose, "3"]
2010  // AFTER: argv = [-rose:verbose, "3"]
2011  // java_options = [-classpath, "/some/class/path"]
2012  std::vector<std::string> java_options =
2013  CommandlineProcessing::generateOptionWithNameParameterList(
2014  argv, // Remove ROSE-Java options from here
2015  Cmdline::Java::option_prefix, // Current prefix
2016  "-"); // New prefix
2017 
2018  for (std::vector<std::string>::iterator it = java_options.begin();
2019  it != java_options.end();
2020  ++it)
2021  {
2022  std::string java_option = *it;
2023 
2024  // Skip ROSE-specific Java options
2025  //
2026  // "-ds": source destination directory for unparsed code is specific to ROSE.
2027  if (java_option == "-ds")
2028  ++it; // skip over argument, i.e. "-ds <argument>"; TODO: add argument verification
2029  else
2030  argv.push_back(java_option);
2031  }
2032 }// Cmdline::Java::StripRoseOptions

2507 Rose_STL_Container<std::string>
2508 Rose::Cmdline::Java::
2509 ExpandArglist (const std::string& arglist_string)
2510 {
2511  ROSE_ASSERT(!arglist_string.empty());
2512  ROSE_ASSERT(arglist_string[0] == '@'); // @filename
2513 
2514  Rose_STL_Container<std::string> arglist;
2515 
2516  if (arglist_string.size() < 2)
2517  {
2518  std::cout
2519  << "[FATAL] No filename found after @ symbol "
2520  << "on the command line. Should be @<filename>."
2521  << std::endl;
2522  ROSE_ABORT();
2523  }
2524  else
2525  {
2526  std::string filename = arglist_string.substr(1);
2527  ROSE_ASSERT(filename.empty() == false);
2528 
2529  arglist = Rose::Cmdline::Java::GetListFromFile(filename);
2530  if (SgProject::get_verbose() > 2)
2531  {
2532  printf ("[INFO] "
2533  "Expanded @%s = '%s'\n",
2534  filename.c_str(),
2535  StringUtility::listToString(arglist).c_str());
2536  }
2537  return arglist;
2538  }
2539 }// Cmdline::Java::ExpandArglist
2540 
2541 // TODO: should we validate that '@arglist' is only
2542 // passed once on the commandline?
2543 Rose_STL_Container<std::string>
2544 Rose::Cmdline::Java::
2545 ExpandArglist (const Rose_STL_Container<std::string>& p_argv)
2546 {
2547  Rose_STL_Container<std::string> argv = p_argv;
2548  Rose_STL_Container<std::string>::iterator i = argv.begin();
2549  while (i != argv.end())
2550  {
2551  std::string argument = *i;
2552  if (argument[0] == '@')
2553  {
2554  Rose_STL_Container<std::string> arglist =
2555  Rose::Cmdline::Java::ExpandArglist(argument);
2556 
2557  // Insert actual list of arguments in-place where @filename was found
2558  int i_offset = std::distance(argv.begin(), i);
2559  argv.erase(i);
2560  argv.insert(argv.end(), arglist.begin(), arglist.end());
2561  i = argv.begin() + i_offset;
2562  }
2563  else
2564  {
2565  ++i; // next commandline argument
2566  }
2567  }
2568  return argv;
2569 }

2571 std::vector<std::string>
2572 Rose::Cmdline::Java::
2573 GetListFromFile (const std::string& filename)
2574 {
2575  ROSE_ASSERT(! filename.empty());
2576 
2577  std::vector<std::string> list;
2578  std::ifstream file(filename.c_str());
2579  std::string line;
2580 
2581  while (!file.fail() && std::getline(file, line))
2582  {
2583  // TOO1 (3/4/2014): Strip quotes surrounding arguments; this is specific
2584  // to how Maven utilizes javac @argfiles, e.g.:
2585  //
2586  // "javac"
2587  // "-target 1.6"
2588  // "-source 1.6"
2589  // "File.java"
2590  //
2591  // TODO: Re-implement since this will not handle the case
2592  // where file paths contain spaces and require quotations:
2593  //
2594  // "javac"
2595  // "C:\ Program Files\Foo Bar Workspace\File.java"
2596  line.erase(
2597  std::remove(line.begin(), line.end(), '\"'),
2598  line.end());
2599  list.push_back(line);
2600  }
2601 
2602  file.close();
2603 
2604  if (list.empty())
2605  {
2606  std::cout
2607  << "[FATAL] No arguments found in file "
2608  << "'" << filename << "'"
2609  << std::endl;
2610  ROSE_ABORT();
2611  }
2612 
2613  return list;
2614 }
2615 
2616 // -rose:java:ecj options have already been transformed by Cmdline::Java::StripRoseOptions.
2617 // Therefore, for example,
2618 //
2619 // -rose:java:ecj:jvm_options
2620 //
2621 // is now actually:
2622 //
2623 // -ecj:jvm_options
2624 //
2625 void
2626 Rose::Cmdline::Java::Ecj::
2627 StripRoseOptions (std::vector<std::string>& argv)
2628 {
2629  if (SgProject::get_verbose() > 1)
2630  {
2631  std::cout
2632  << "[INFO] "
2633  << "Stripping ROSE Java ECJ commandline options"
2634  << std::endl;
2635  }
2636 
2637  // (1) Options WITHOUT an argument
2638  sla(argv, "-rose:java:ecj:", "($)", "batch_mode", 1);
2639 
2640  //
2641  // (2) Options WITH an argument
2642  //
2643 
2644  // Remove ECJ options with ROSE-ECJ prefix; option arguments removed
2645  // by generateOptionWithNameParameterList.
2646  std::vector<std::string> ecj_options =
2647  CommandlineProcessing::generateOptionWithNameParameterList(
2648  argv, // Remove ROSE-Java options from here
2649  "-ecj:", // Current prefix
2650  "-"); // New prefix
2651 
2652  // TOO1 (2/11/2014): Skip ALL ROSE-specific ECJ options;
2653  // at this stage, we only have "-rose:java:ecj:jvm_options",
2654  // and this is only inteded for the ECJ frontend's JVM.
2655  for (std::string ecj_option : ecj_options)
2656  {
2657  if (SgProject::get_verbose() > 1)
2658  {
2659  std::cout
2660  << "[INFO] "
2661  << "Stripping ECJ JVM commandline argument '" << ecj_option << "'"
2662  << std::endl;
2663  }
2664  }
2665 }// Cmdline::Java::StripRoseOptions

2667 std::string
2668 Rose::Cmdline::Java::Ecj::
2669 GetRoseClasspath ()
2670 {
2671 
2672 #ifdef _MSC_VER
2673  std::string separator = ";";
2674 #else
2675  std::string separator = ":";
2676 #endif
2677 
2678  std::string classpath = "-Djava.class.path=";
2679 
2680  // Java (ECJ front-end) support (adding specific jar file)
2681  std::string ecj_jar_file_name = std::string("ecj-3.8.2.jar");
2682  std::string ecj_class_path_jarfile =
2683  "src/3rdPartyLibraries/java-parser/" +
2684  ecj_jar_file_name;
2685 
2686  classpath +=
2687  findRoseSupportPathFromBuild(
2688  ecj_class_path_jarfile,
2689  std::string("lib/") + ecj_jar_file_name
2690  );
2691  classpath += separator;
2692 
2693  // Java (ECJ front-end) support (adding path to source tree for the jar file).
2694  // This allows us to avoid copying the jar file to the build tree which is
2695  // write protected in the execution of the "make distcheck" rule.
2696  std::string ecj_class_path = "src/3rdPartyLibraries/java-parser/";
2697  classpath +=
2698  findRoseSupportPathFromBuild(
2699  ecj_class_path,
2700  std::string("lib/"));
2701  classpath += separator;
2702 
2703  // Everything else?
2704  classpath += ".";
2705 
2706  return classpath;
2707 }

2817 void
2818 SgFile::usage ( int status )
2819  {
2820  if (status != 0)
2821  fprintf (stderr,"Try option `--help' for more information.\n");
2822  else
2823  {
2824  // it would be nice to insert the version of ROSE being used (using the VERSION macro)
2825  fputs(
2826 "\n"
2827 "This ROSE translator provides a means for operating on Ada, C, C++, Fortran and Java\n"
2828 "source code; as well as on x86, ARM, and PowerPC executable code (plus object files \n"
2829 "and libraries).\n"
2830 "\n"
2831 "Usage: rose [OPTION]... FILENAME...\n"
2832 "\n"
2833 "If a long option shows a mandatory argument, it is mandatory for the equivalent\n"
2834 "short option as well, and similarly for optional arguments.\n"
2835 "\n"
2836 "Main operation mode:\n"
2837 " -rose:(o|output) FILENAME\n"
2838 " file containing final unparsed C++ code\n"
2839 " (relative or absolute paths are supported)\n"
2840 " -rose:keep_going\n"
2841 " Similar to GNU Make's --keep-going option.\n"
2842 "\n"
2843 " If ROSE encounters an error while processing your\n"
2844 " input code, ROSE will simply run your backend compiler on\n"
2845 " your original source code file, as is, without modification.\n"
2846 "\n"
2847 " This is useful for compiler tests. For example,\n"
2848 " when compiling a 100K LOC application, you can\n"
2849 " try to compile as much as possible, ignoring failures,\n"
2850 " in order to gauage the overall status of your translator,\n"
2851 " with respect to that application.\n"
2852 "\n"
2853 "Operation modifiers:\n"
2854 " -rose:output_warnings compile with warnings mode on\n"
2855 " -rose:C_only, -rose:C follow C89 standard, disable C++\n"
2856 " -rose:C89_only, -rose:C89\n"
2857 " follow C89 standard, disable C++\n"
2858 " -rose:C99_only, -rose:C99\n"
2859 " follow C99 standard, disable C++\n"
2860 " -rose:C11_only, -rose:C11\n"
2861 " follow C11 standard, disable C++\n"
2862 " -rose:C17_only, -rose:C17\n"
2863 " follow C17 standard, disable C++\n"
2864 " -rose:C23_only, -rose:C23\n"
2865 " follow C23 standard, disable C++\n"
2866 " -rose:C2y_only, -rose:C2y\n"
2867 " follow C2y standard, disable C++\n"
2868 " -rose:Cxx_only, -rose:Cxx\n"
2869 " follow C++89 standard\n"
2870 " -rose:Cxx11_only, -rose:Cxx11\n"
2871 " follow C++11 standard\n"
2872 " -rose:Cxx14_only, -rose:Cxx14\n"
2873 " follow C++14 standard\n"
2874 " -rose:Cxx17_only, -rose:Cxx17\n"
2875 " follow C++17 standard\n"
2876 " -rose:Cxx20_only, -rose:Cxx20\n"
2877 " follow C++20 standard\n"
2878 " -rose:Cxx23_only, -rose:Cxx23\n"
2879 " follow C++23 standard\n"
2880 " -rose:Cxx26_only, -rose:Cxx26\n"
2881 " follow C++26 standard\n"
2882 " -rose:java\n"
2883 " compile Java code (work in progress)\n"
2884 " -rose:java:cp, -rose:java:classpath, -cp, -classpath\n"
2885 " Classpath to look for java classes\n"

2887 " Sourcepath to look for java sources\n"

2900 // " -rose:java:Xms<size>\n"

2904 // " -rose:java:Xss<size>\n"

2906 " -rose:Python, -rose:python, -rose:py\n"
2907 " compile Python code\n"
2908 " -rose:OpenMP, -rose:openmp\n"
2909 " follow OpenMP 3.0 specification for C/C++ and Fortran, perform one of the following actions:\n"
2910 " -rose:OpenMP:parse_only, -rose:openmp:parse_only\n"
2911 " parse OpenMP directives to OmpAttributes, no further actions (default behavior now)\n"
2912 " -rose:OpenMP:ast_only, -rose:openmp:ast_only\n"
2913 " on top of -rose:openmp:parse_only, build OpenMP AST nodes from OmpAttributes, no further actions\n"

2915 " on top of -rose:openmp:ast_only, transform AST with OpenMP nodes into multithreaded code \n"

2918 " follow OpenACC 3.0 specification for Fortran, perform one of the following actions:\n"
2919 " -rose:OpenACC:parse_only, -rose:openacc:parse_only\n"
2920 " parse OpenACC directives to OmpAccAttributes, no further actions (default behavior now)\n"
2921 " -rose:OpenACC:ast_only, -rose:openacc:ast_only\n"
2922 " on top of -rose:openacc:parse_only, build OpenACC AST nodes from OmpAccAttributes, no further actions\n"
2923 " -rose:UPC_only, -rose:UPC\n"
2924 " follow Unified Parallel C 1.2 specification\n"
2925 " -rose:UPCxx_only, -rose:UPCxx\n"

2929 " -rose:upc_threads n Enable UPC static threads compilation with n threads\n"
2930 " n>=1: static threads; dynamic(default) otherwise\n"
2931 " -rose:fortran\n"
2932 " compile Fortran code, determining version of\n"
2933 " Fortran from file suffix)\n"
2934 " -rose:CoArrayFortran, -rose:CAF, -rose:caf\n"
2935 " compile Co-Array Fortran code (extension of Fortran 2003)\n"
2936 " -rose:CAF2.0, -rose:caf2.0\n"

2945 " compile Fortran 77 code\n"
2946 " -rose:Fortran66, -rose:F66, -rose:f66\n"
2947 " compile Fortran 66 code\n"
2948 " -rose:FortranIV, -rose:FIV, -rose:fIV\n"
2949 " compile Fortran IV code\n"
2950 " -rose:FortranII, -rose:FII, -rose:fII\n"
2951 " compile Fortran II code (not implemented yet)\n"
2952 " -rose:FortranI, -rose:FI, -rose:fI\n"
2953 " compile Fortran I code (not implemented yet)\n"
2954 " -rose:fortran:ofp:jvm_options\n"

2956 " -rose:strict strict enforcement of ANSI/ISO standards\n"
2957 " -rose:binary, -rose:binary_only\n"
2958 " assume input file is for binary analysis (this avoids\n"
2959 " ambiguity when ROSE might want to assume linking instead)\n"
2960 " -rose:FailSafe, -rose:failsafe\n"
2961 " Enable experimental processing of resilience directives defined by FAIL-SAFE annotation language specification.\n"
2962 " -rose:projectSpecificDatabaseFile FILE\n"

3335 void
3336 SgFile::processRoseCommandLineOptions ( vector<string> & argv )
3337  {
3338  // Strip out the rose specific command line options
3339  // then search for all filenames (options without the "-" prefix)
3340  // the assume all other arguments are to be passed onto the C or C++ compiler
3341 
3342  // Split out the ROSE options first
3343 
3344  //
3345  // help option (allows alternative -h or -help instead of just -rose:help)
3346  // This is the only rose options that does not require the "-rose:" prefix
3347  //
3348  if ( CommandlineProcessing::isOption(argv,"-rose:","(h|help)",true) == true ||
3349  CommandlineProcessing::isOption(argv,"--", "(h|help)",true) == true ||
3350  CommandlineProcessing::isOption(argv,"-","(h|help)",true) == true )
3351  {
3352  cout << version_message() << endl;
3353  usage(0);
3354  }
3355 
3356  //
3357  // Diagnostic logging. We need all of the '-rose:log WHAT' command-line switches in the order they appear, which seems to
3358  // mean that we need to parse the argv vector ourselves. CommandlineParsing doesn't have a suitable function, and the sla
3359  // code in sla++.C is basically unreadable and its minimal documentation doesn't seem to match its macro-hidden API,
3360  // specifically the part about being able to return an array of values.
3361  //
3362  Rose::initialize(nullptr);
3363  static const std::string removalString = "(--REMOVE_ME--)";
3364  for (size_t i=0; i<argv.size(); ++i) {
3365  if ((0==strcmp(argv[i].c_str(), "-rose:log")) && i+1 < argv.size()) {
3366  argv[i] = removalString;
3367  std::string switchValue = argv[++i];
3368  argv[i] = removalString;
3369 
3370  // This is a bit of a roundabout way to do this, but it supports "help", "list", etc and keeps ROSE's capabilities
3371  // up to date with the latest documentation in Sawyer.
3372  using namespace Sawyer::CommandLine;
3373  SwitchGroup switches;
3374  switches.insert(Switch("rose:log")
3375  .resetLongPrefixes("-") // ROSE switches only support single hyphens
3376  .action(configureDiagnostics("rose:log", Diagnostics::mfacilities))
3377  .argument("config"));
3378  std::vector<std::string> args;
3379  args.push_back("-rose:log");
3380  args.push_back(switchValue);
3381  Parser parser;
3382  parser.with(switches).parse(args).apply(); // causes configureDiagnostics to be called
3383  }
3384  }
3385  argv.erase(std::remove(argv.begin(), argv.end(), removalString), argv.end());
3386 
3387  //
3388  // -rose:assert abort|exit|throw
3389  //
3390  for (size_t i=0; i<argv.size(); ++i) {
3391  if (argv[i] == std::string("-rose:assert") && i+1 < argv.size()) {
3392  std::string switchValue = argv[i+1];
3393  Sawyer::Assert::AssertFailureHandler handler = nullptr;
3394  if (switchValue == "abort") {
3395  handler = Rose::abortOnFailedAssertion;
3396  } else if (switchValue == "exit") {
3397  handler = Rose::exitOnFailedAssertion;
3398  } else if (switchValue == "throw") {
3399  handler = Rose::throwOnFailedAssertion;
3400  }
3401  if (handler != nullptr) {
3402  argv[i] = argv[i+1] = removalString;
3403  Rose::failedAssertionBehavior(handler);
3404  }
3405  }
3406  }
3407  argv.erase(std::remove(argv.begin(), argv.end(), removalString), argv.end());
3408 
3409  //
3410  // markGeneratedFiles option
3411  //
3412  set_markGeneratedFiles(false);
3413  if ( CommandlineProcessing::isOption(argv,"-rose:","(markGeneratedFiles)",true) == true )
3414  {
3415  // Optionally mark the generated files with "#define ROSE_GENERATED_CODE"
3416  set_markGeneratedFiles(true);
3417  }
3418 
3419  //

4319  // Fixed format v.s. free format option handling (ROSE defaults to fix or free format, depending on the file extension).
4320  // F77 default is fixed format, F90 and later default is free format.
4321  // Fortran source file format options for different compilers(for IBM/XL,Intel,Portland,GNU):
4322  // IBM/XL Intel Portland GNU
4323  // -qfixed -fixed -Mfixed -ffixed-form
4324  // -qfree -free -Mfree -free-form
4325  // GNU gfortran also supports -fno-fixed-form (we could use this to turn off all fixed form
4326  // formatting independent of the input source).
4327 
4328  if (get_F77_only() == true)
4329  {
4330  // Use the setting get_F77_only() == true as a default means to set this value
4331  set_inputFormat(SgFile::e_fixed_form_output_format);

4336  {
4337  // Use the setting get_F77_only() == true as a default means to set this value
4338  set_inputFormat(SgFile::e_free_form_output_format);
4339  set_outputFormat(SgFile::e_free_form_output_format);
4340  set_backendCompileFormat(SgFile::e_free_form_output_format);

4429  // Liao 3/12/2020: handle options for OpenACC support
4430  // Allows handling of OpenACC "!$omp" directives in free form and "c$omp", *$omp and "!$omp" directives in fixed form, enables "!$" conditional
4431  // compilation sentinels in free form and "c$", "*$" and "!$" sentinels in fixed form and when linking arranges for the OpenMP runtime library
4432  // to be linked in. (Not implemented yet).
4433  set_openacc(false);
4434  string ompacc_macro="-D_OPENACC="+ StringUtility::numberToString(3);
4435  ROSE_ASSERT (get_openacc() == false);
4436  ROSE_ASSERT (get_openacc_parse_only() == false);
4437  ROSE_ASSERT (get_openacc_ast_only() == false);
4438  if ( CommandlineProcessing::isOption(argv,"-rose:","(OpenACC|openacc)",true) == true
4439  ||CommandlineProcessing::isOption(argv,"-","(acc|openacc|fopenacc)",true) == true
4440  )
4441  {
4442  if ( SgProject::get_verbose() >= 1 )
4443  printf ("OpenACC option specified \n");
4444  set_openacc(true);
4445  set_openacc_parse_only(true); // default is parse_only for now
4446  //side effect for enabling OpenACC, define the macro as required
4447  //This new option does not reach the backend compiler
4448  //But it is enough to reach EDG only.
4449  //We can later on back end option to turn on their OpenMP handling flags,
4450  //like -fopenacc for GCC, depending on the version of gcc
4451  //which will define this macro for GCC
4452  argv.push_back(ompacc_macro);
4453  }
4454 
4455  // Process sub-options
4456  // We want to turn on OpenACC if any of its suboptions is used.
4457  if ( CommandlineProcessing::isOption(argv,"-rose:OpenACC:","parse_only",true) == true
4458  ||CommandlineProcessing::isOption(argv,"-rose:openacc:","parse_only",true) == true
4459  ||CommandlineProcessing::isOption(argv,"--rose:OpenACC:","parse_only",true) == true
4460  ||CommandlineProcessing::isOption(argv,"--rose:openacc:","parse_only",true) == true
4461  )

4890  //

4893  // the memory (from new allocations) previously deleted. A later leve of this option will disable
4894  // reuse of previously deleted memory for IR nodes; but it will consume more memory for translators
4895  // that delete a lot of IR nodes as part of there functionality. I expect this to only seriously
4896  // make a difference for the AST merge operations which allocate and delete large parts of ASTs
4897  // frequently.

4899  //

4902  {

4906  {
4907  integerDebugOption = 1;
4908  if ( SgProject::get_verbose() >= 1 )
4909  printf ("option -rose:detect_dangling_pointers found but value not specified or set to 0 default (reset integerDebugOption = %d) \n",integerDebugOption);
4910  }
4911  else
4912  {
4913  if ( SgProject::get_verbose() >= 1 )
4914  printf ("option -rose:detect_dangling_pointers found with level (integerDebugOption = %d) \n",integerDebugOption);
4915  }

4973  p_skip_unparse = true;
4974  p_skipfinalCompileStep = true;
4975  break;
4976  case 4 :
4977  // all of 3 (above) plus parse into SAGE program tree
4978  // p_skip_buildHigherLevelGrammars = true;
4979  p_skip_transformation = true;
4980  p_skip_unparse = true;
4981  p_skipfinalCompileStep = true;
4982  break;
4983  case 5 :
4984  // all of 4 (above) plus unparse to generate (untransformed source code)
4985  // p_skip_buildHigherLevelGrammars = true;
4986  p_skip_transformation = true;
4987  p_skipfinalCompileStep = true;
4988  break;
4989  case 6 :
4990  // all of 4 (above) plus compile generated source code
4991  // p_skip_buildHigherLevelGrammars = true;
4992  p_skip_transformation = true;
4993  break;
4994  case 7 :
4995  // all of 5 (above) plus parse into higher level grammars before unparsing
4996  p_skip_transformation = true;
4997  p_skipfinalCompileStep = true;
4998  break;
4999  case 8 :
5000  // all of 7 (above) plus compile resulting unparsed code (without transformations)
5001  p_skip_transformation = true;
5002  break;
5003  case 9 :
5004  // all of 8 (above) plus run transformations before unparsing (do everything)
5005  break;
5006  default:
5007  // default mode is an error
5008  printf ("Default reached in processing -rose:test # option (use 0-6, input option = %d) \n",integerOption);
5009  ROSE_ABORT();
5010  break;
5011  }
5012  }
5013 
5014  //
5015  // new_unparser option
5016  //
5017  if ( CommandlineProcessing::isOption(argv,"-rose:","(skipfinalCompileStep)",true) == true )
5018  {
5019  if (get_verbose()>0) // Liao, 8/29/2008, Only show it in verbose mode.
5020  printf ("option -rose:skipfinalCompileStep found \n");
5021  set_skipfinalCompileStep(true);
5022  }
5023 
5024  //
5025  // Standard compiler options (allows alternative -E option to just run CPP)
5026  //
5027  if ( CommandlineProcessing::isOption(argv,"-","(E)",true) == true )
5028  {
5029  p_useBackendOnly = true;
5030  p_disable_edg_backend = true; // This variable should be called frontend NOT backend???
5031  p_skip_transformation = true;
5032  p_skip_unparse = true;
5033  p_skipfinalCompileStep = false;
5034 
5035  // DQ (8/22/2009): Verify that this was set when the command line was processed at the SgProject level.
5036  SgProject* project = this->get_project();
5037  ASSERT_not_null(project);
5038  ROSE_ASSERT(project->get_C_PreprocessorOnly() == true);
5039  }
5040 
5041  // DQ (1/19/2014): This option "-S" is required for some build systems (e.g. valgrind).
5042  //
5043  // Standard compiler options (allows alternative -S option to just run with gcc)
5044  //
5045  if ( CommandlineProcessing::isOption(argv,"-","(S)",true) == true )
5046  {
5047  p_useBackendOnly = true;
5048  p_disable_edg_backend = true; // This variable should be called frontend NOT backend???
5049  p_skip_transformation = true;
5050  p_skip_unparse = true;
5051  p_skipfinalCompileStep = false;
5052 
5053  // DQ (8/22/2009): Verify that this was set when the command line was processed at the SgProject level.
5054  SgProject* project = this->get_project();
5055  ASSERT_not_null(project);
5056  ROSE_ASSERT(project->get_stop_after_compilation_do_not_assemble_file() == true);
5057  }
5058 
5059  //
5060  // Standard compiler options (allows alternative -H option to just output header file info)
5061  //
5062  if ( CommandlineProcessing::isOption(argv,"-","(H)",true) == true )
5063  {
5064  // DQ (1/23/2018): Note, we can call the backend compiler using -H or call edg with -H.
5065  // This option will call the backend compiler with -H, if we want to call edg with -H
5066  // then we use -edg:H as the option to ROSE.
5067  p_useBackendOnly = true;
5068  p_disable_edg_backend = true; // This variable should be called frontend NOT backend???
5069  p_skip_transformation = true;
5070  p_skip_unparse = true;
5071  p_skipfinalCompileStep = false;
5072  }
5073 
5074  //
5075  // negative_test option: allows passing all tests to be treated as an error!
5076  //
5077  if ( CommandlineProcessing::isOption(argv,"-rose:","(negative_test)",true) == true )
5078  {
5079  printf ("option -rose:negative_test found \n");
5080  set_negative_test(true);
5081  }
5082 
5083  //
5084  // We have processed all rose supported command line options.
5085  // Anything left in argv now should be a typo or option for either EDG or the C or C++ compiler.
5086  //
5087  if ( get_verbose() > 1 )
5088  {
5089  cout << "The remaining non-rose options will be passed onto either the parser/front-end or the backend (vendor) the compiler: " << endl;
5090  for (unsigned int i = 1; i < argv.size(); i++)
5091  {
5092  cout << " argv[" << i << "]= " << argv[i] << endl;
5093  }
5094  }
5095  }

5461 Rose_STL_Container<string>
5462 CommandlineProcessing::generateOptionListWithDeclaredParameters (const Rose_STL_Container<string> & argList, string inputPrefix )
5463  {
5464  // This function returns a list of options using the inputPrefix (with the inputPrefix stripped off).
5465  Rose_STL_Container<string> optionList;
5466  unsigned int prefixLength = inputPrefix.length();
5467  for (Rose_STL_Container<string>::const_iterator i = argList.begin(); i != argList.end(); i++)
5468  {
5469  if ( (*i).substr(0,prefixLength) == inputPrefix )
5470  {
5471  // get the rest of the string as the option
5472  string option = (*i).substr(prefixLength);
5473  optionList.push_back(option);
5474  if (isOptionTakingSecondParameter(*i)) {
5475  i++;
5476  optionList.push_back(*i);
5477  }
5478  }
5479  }
5480  return optionList;
5481  }

5509 SgFile::processBackendSpecificCommandLineOptions ( const vector<string>& argvOrig )
5510  {
5511  // DQ (6/21/2005): This function processes commandline options that are specific to the backend
5512  // but which the front-end or ROSE should know about. Examples include template options that
5513  // would influence how ROSE instantiates or outputs templates in the code generation phase.

5520  // -ansi option (fairly general option name across a number of compilers, I think)

5524  set_strict_language_handling(true);

5537 
5538  //
5539  // -fno-implicit-inline-templates option
5540  //

5542  if ( CommandlineProcessing::isOption(argv,"-f","no-implicit-inline-templates",true) == true )
5543  {
5544  // don't instantiate any inline templates

5551 void
5552 SgFile::build_CLANG_CommandLine(vector<string> &inputCommandLine, vector<string> &argv, int /*fileNameIndex*/) {
5553  // It filters Rose and Edg specific parameters and fixes the paths.
5554 
5555  std::vector<std::string> inc_dirs_list;
5556  std::vector<std::string> define_list;
5557  std::string input_file;
5558 
5559  for (size_t i = 0; i < argv.size(); i++) {
5560  std::string current_arg(argv[i]);
5561  if (current_arg.find("-I") == 0) {
5562  if (current_arg.length() > 2) {
5563  inc_dirs_list.push_back(current_arg.substr(2));
5564  }
5565  else {
5566  i++;
5567  if (i < argv.size())
5568  inc_dirs_list.push_back(current_arg);
5569  else
5570  break;
5571  }
5572  }
5573  else if (current_arg.find("-D") == 0) {
5574  if (current_arg.length() > 2) {
5575  define_list.push_back(current_arg.substr(2));
5576  }
5577  else {
5578  i++;
5579  if (i < argv.size())
5580  define_list.push_back(current_arg);
5581  else
5582  break;
5583  }
5584  }
5585  else if (current_arg.find("-c") == 0) {}
5586  else if (current_arg.find("-o") == 0) {
5587  if (current_arg.length() == 2) {
5588  i++;
5589  if (i >= argv.size()) break;
5590  }
5591  }
5592  else if (current_arg.find("-rose") == 0) {}
5593  else {
5594  input_file = current_arg;
5595  }
5596  }
5597 
5598  std::vector<std::string>::iterator it_str;
5599  for (it_str = define_list.begin(); it_str != define_list.end(); it_str++)
5600  inputCommandLine.push_back("-D" + *it_str);
5601  for (it_str = inc_dirs_list.begin(); it_str != inc_dirs_list.end(); it_str++)
5602  inputCommandLine.push_back("-I" + StringUtility::getAbsolutePathFromRelativePath(*it_str));
5603 
5604  std::string input_file_path = StringUtility::getPathFromFileName(input_file);
5605  input_file = StringUtility::stripPathFromFileName(input_file);
5606  if (input_file_path == "" ) input_file_path = "./";
5607  input_file_path = StringUtility::getAbsolutePathFromRelativePath(input_file_path);
5608  input_file = input_file_path + "/" + input_file;
5609  inputCommandLine.push_back(input_file);
5610 
5611 }

5613 void
5614 SgFile::build_EDG_CommandLine ( vector<string> & inputCommandLine, vector<string> & argv, int fileNameIndex )
5615  {
5616  // This function builds the command line input for the edg_main (the EDG C++ Front-End)
5617  // There are numerous options that must be set for different architectures. We can find
5618  // a more general setup of these options within something like Duct-Tape. In this function
5619  // argv and argc are the parameters from the user's commandline, and inputCommandLine and
5620  // numberOfCommandLineArguments are parameters for the new command line that will be build
5621  // for EDG.
5622 
5623  ROSE_ASSERT(get_file_info()->get_filenameString() == get_sourceFileNameWithPath());
5624  ROSE_ASSERT(fileNameIndex == 0);
5625 
5626 #if !defined(CXX_SPEC_DEF)
5627  // Output an error and exit
5628  cout << "ERROR: The preprocessor definition CXX_SPEC_DEF should have been defined by the configure process!!" << endl;
5629  ROSE_ABORT();
5630 #endif
5631 
5632  const char* configDefsArray[] = CXX_SPEC_DEF;
5633  const char* Cxx_ConfigIncludeDirsRaw[] = CXX_INCLUDE_STRING;
5634  const char* C_ConfigIncludeDirsRaw[] = C_INCLUDE_STRING;
5635  Rose_STL_Container<string> configDefs(configDefsArray, configDefsArray + sizeof(configDefsArray) / sizeof(*configDefsArray));
5636  Rose_STL_Container<string> Cxx_ConfigIncludeDirs(Cxx_ConfigIncludeDirsRaw, Cxx_ConfigIncludeDirsRaw + sizeof(Cxx_ConfigIncludeDirsRaw) / sizeof(const char*));
5637  Rose_STL_Container<string> C_ConfigIncludeDirs(C_ConfigIncludeDirsRaw, C_ConfigIncludeDirsRaw + sizeof(C_ConfigIncludeDirsRaw) / sizeof(const char*));
5638 
5639 #if 0
5640 #error "DEAD CODE!"
5641 // DQ (7/3/2013): This is a work around to support a bug in EDG 4.7 which causes test2013_246.C to fail (boost example code).
5642 #if __GNUC__ > 4 || (__GNUC__ == 4 && (__GNUC_MINOR__ > 3 || (__GNUC_MINOR__ == 3 && __GNUC_PATCHLEVEL__ >= 0)))
5643 #error "DEAD CODE!"
5644  // DQ (7/3/2013): For this to let EDG think we have a GNU 4.2 compiler.
5645  ROSE_ASSERT(configDefs.size() >= 3);
5646  configDefs[0] = "-D__GNUG__=4";
5647  configDefs[1] = "-D__GNUC__=4";
5648  configDefs[2] = "-D__GNUC_MINOR__=2";
5649 #error "DEAD CODE!"
5650 
5651 // DQ (7/3/2013): This macro is used in rose_edg_required_macros_and_functions.h.in (temporary work about for EDG 4.7).
5652 #error "DEAD CODE!"
5653 #define LIE_ABOUT_GNU_VERSION_TO_EDG
5654 #error "DEAD CODE!"
5655 #endif
5656 #error "DEAD CODE!"
5657 #else
5658 #endif
5659 
5660  // Removed reference to __restrict__ so it could be placed into the preinclude vendor specific header file for ROSE.
5661  // DQ (9/10/2004): Attept to add support for restrict (but I think this just sets it to true, using "-Dxxx=" works)
5662  // const string roseSpecificDefs = "-DUSE_RESTRICT_POINTERS_IN_ROSE_TRANSFORMATIONS -DUSE_ROSE -D__restrict__=";
5663  vector<string> roseSpecificDefs;
5664 
5665  // Communicate that ROSE transformation can use the restrict keyword.
5666  roseSpecificDefs.push_back("-DUSE_RESTRICT_POINTERS_IN_ROSE_TRANSFORMATIONS");
5667 
5668  // Communicate to the generated program that we are using ROSE (in case there are specific options that the user wants to to invoke.
5669  roseSpecificDefs.push_back("-DUSE_ROSE");
5670 
5671  ROSE_ASSERT(configDefs.empty() == false);
5672  ROSE_ASSERT(Cxx_ConfigIncludeDirs.empty() == false);
5673  ROSE_ASSERT(C_ConfigIncludeDirs.empty() == false);
5674 
5675  vector<string> commandLine;
5676 
5677 #ifdef ROSE_USE_MICROSOFT_EXTENSIONS
5678  // DQ (4/21/2014): Add Microsoft specific options:
5679  // --microsoft
5680  // --microsoft_16
5681  // --microsoft_version version-number
5682  // --microsoft_build_number build-number
5683  // Not all of these are required, the simplest usage is to use "--microsoft".
5684  // DQ (4/21/2014): Use the simple option to turn on microsoft mode.
5685  commandLine.push_back("--microsoft");
5686 #endif
5687 
5688 #ifndef ROSE_USE_MICROSOFT_EXTENSIONS
5689 #ifndef _MSC_VER
5690  // DQ (4/13/2016): This must use the values of __GNUC__, __GNUC_MINOR__, and __GNUC_PATCHLEVEL__
5691  // from the backend compiler. Note that we don't save the __GNUC_PATCHLEVEL__ for the backend
5692  // compiler, but we can assume it is zero (I think this should work well).
5693  // DQ (7/3/2013): We don't have to lie to EDG about the version of GNU that it should emulate
5694  // (only to the parts of Boost the read the GNU compiler version number information).
5695  // DQ (7/3/2013): Adding option to specify the version of GNU to emulate.
5696  // int emulate_gnu_version_number = __GNUC__*10000 + __GNUC_MINOR__*100 + __GNUC_PATCHLEVEL__;
5697  // int emulate_gnu_version_number = BACKEND_CXX_COMPILER_MAJOR_VERSION_NUMBER*10000 + BACKEND_CXX_COMPILER_MINOR_VERSION_NUMBER*100 + 0;
5698  int emulate_backend_compiler_version_number = BACKEND_CXX_COMPILER_MAJOR_VERSION_NUMBER*10000 + BACKEND_CXX_COMPILER_MINOR_VERSION_NUMBER*100 + 0;
5699 
5700 #ifdef BACKEND_CXX_IS_INTEL_COMPILER
5701  // DQ (9/6/2015): Reset to specific version of GNU for Intel v14 compiler.
5702  // emulate_backend_compiler_version_number = 4*10000 + 8*100 + 3;
5703 
5704  // DQ (12/13/2016): Test tis for Intel v16.
5705  emulate_backend_compiler_version_number = 6*10000 + 1*100 + 0;

5707 
5708  // DQ (7/3/2014): Testing if we emulate a different version of GNU g++.
5709  // emulate_backend_compiler_version_number = 4*10000 + 8*100 + 1;
5710 
5711  if (SgProject::get_verbose() > 0)
5712  {
5713  printf ("In SgFile::build_EDG_CommandLine(): emulate_backend_compiler_version_number = %d \n",emulate_backend_compiler_version_number);

5716  // DQ (4/26/2019): NOTE: this option appears to be incompatable with use of gnu_version.
5717  if (get_strict_language_handling() == false)
5718  {
5719 #ifdef BACKEND_CXX_IS_INTEL_COMPILER
5720  commandLine.push_back("--gnu_version");
5721 #endif
5722 
5723 #ifdef BACKEND_CXX_IS_GNU_COMPILER
5724  commandLine.push_back("--gnu_version");

5726  #ifdef USE_CMAKE
5727  // DQ (4/20/2016): When using CMAKE the BACKEND_CXX_IS_GNU_COMPILER is not defiled.
5728  commandLine.push_back("--gnu_version");
5729  #endif
5730 #endif
5731 
5732 #ifdef BACKEND_CXX_IS_CLANG_COMPILER
5733  commandLine.push_back("--clang");
5734  commandLine.push_back("--clang_version");
5735 #endif
5736  commandLine.push_back(StringUtility::numberToString(emulate_backend_compiler_version_number));
5737  }
5738 #endif
5739 #endif
5740 
5741 #ifdef LIE_ABOUT_GNU_VERSION_TO_EDG
5742  // DQ (7/3/2013): define this so that the rose_edg_required_macros_and_functions.h header file can make
5743  // some builtin function available (required to compile test2013_246.C).
5744  commandLine.push_back("-DLIE_ABOUT_GNU_VERSION_TO_EDG");
5745 #endif
5746 
5747  // DQ (6/13/2013): This was wrong, the parent of the SgFile is the SgFileList IR node and it is better to call the function to get the SgProject.
5748  // SgProject* project = isSgProject(this->get_parent());
5749  SgProject* project = TransformationSupport::getProject(this);
5750  ASSERT_not_null(project);
5751 
5752  // AS(063006) Changed implementation so that real paths can be found later
5753  vector<string> includePaths;
5754 
5755  // DQ (1.20/2014): Adding support for -m32 and associated macro to ROSE to force size_t to be defined to be 32-bit instead of 64-bit.
5756  if (project->get_mode_32_bit() == true)
5757  {
5758  roseSpecificDefs.push_back("-DROSE_M32BIT");
5759  }
5760 
5761  // skip the 0th entry since this is just the name of the program (e.g. rose)
5762  for (unsigned int i=1; i < argv.size(); i++)
5763  {
5764  // most options appear as -<option>
5765  // have to process +w2 (warnings option) on some compilers so include +<option>
5766  if ( argv[i].size() >= 2 && (argv[i][0] == '-') && (argv[i][1] == 'I') )
5767  {
5768  // AS: Did changes to get absolute path
5769  std::string includeDirectorySpecifier = argv[i].substr(2);
5770  includeDirectorySpecifier = StringUtility::getAbsolutePathFromRelativePath(includeDirectorySpecifier );
5771  includePaths.push_back(includeDirectorySpecifier);
5772  }
5773  }
5774 
5775 #ifndef ROSE_USE_MICROSOFT_EXTENSIONS
5776  commandLine.insert(commandLine.end(), configDefs.begin(), configDefs.end());
5777 #else
5778  // DQ (4/21/2014): The preinclude file we generate for ROSE is specific to the backend and for Windows code might be too specific to Linux.
5779  // But we certainly don't want the -D options: e.g "-D__GNUG__=4 -D__GNUC__=4 -D__GNUC_MINOR__=4 -D__GNUC_PATCHLEVEL__=7"
5780  commandLine.push_back("--preinclude");
5781  commandLine.push_back("rose_edg_required_macros_and_functions.h");

5784  commandLine.push_back("-DROSE_USE_MICROSOFT_EXTENSIONS");
5785 #endif

5787  // DQ (5/24/2015): Adding support for specification of optimization to trigger use of __OPTIMIZE__ macro (required for compatability with GNU gcc API).
5788  if (get_optimization() == true && get_no_optimize_flag_for_frontend() == false)
5789  {
5790  commandLine.push_back("-D__OPTIMIZE__");
5791  }

5793  // DQ (3/14/2015): This has been moved to before the compiler and system specific include and
5794  // sys_include paths so that header files with names that match compiler and system header
5795  // files will be used instead from the directories specified using the -I and sys_include options.
5796  // Note that this bug fix is required to support Xen (which uses it's own header files that have
5797  // the same name as system and compiler specific header files).
5798 
5799  // Add the -I definitions to the command line
5800  for (vector<string>::const_iterator i = includePaths.begin(); i != includePaths.end(); ++i)
5801  {
5802  // inputCommandLine.push_back("-I" + *i);
5803  commandLine.push_back("-I" + *i);
5804  }

5806  // PL (4/15/2014): In GCC's document about system headers (http://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/cpp/System-Headers.html):
5807  // All directories named by -isystem are searched after all directories named by -I, no matter what their order was on the command line.
5808  // DQ (4/14/2014): Experiment with placing this here (after "-I" options). This is part of the
5809  // fix to supress redundant output of all "-i" paths as "-sys_include" options to EDG.
5810  if ( SgProject::get_verbose() > 1 )
5811  {
5812  printf ("project->get_preincludeDirectoryList().size() = %" PRIuPTR " \n",project->get_preincludeDirectoryList().size());
5813  }

6367  // DQ (12/18/2016): Add support to use the EDG frontend within ROSE to process the inout file and output the preprocessed version.
6368  // However, we want to suppress the output of declarations from our ROSE preinclude file, so that the output can be processed by ROSE.
6369  // In the case of the Intel comiler, we also want to include "-D__INTEL_CLANG_COMPILER" so that we take the simple trip through the
6370  // Intel comiler's header files that avoids complex builtin function handling (builtin functions that reference types defined in the
6371  // header files and which we could not define in our ROSE preinclude file).
6372  Rose_STL_Container<string>::iterator j = edgOptionList.begin();
6373  while (j != edgOptionList.end())
6374  {
6375  if (*j == "E")
6376  {
6377  // This is the EDG option "-E" obtained from the ROSE "-edg:E" option
6378 
6379  // We want to add the USE_ROSE_CPP_PROCESSING
6380  // CommandlineProcessing::addListToCommandLine(inputCommandLine,"-",edgOptionList);
6381 
6382  // Specify that we are using ROSE to process the input file using CPP (so that in our preinclude file we can skip all ROSE specific declarations.

6385 #ifdef BACKEND_CXX_IS_INTEL_COMPILER

6387  // add -D__INTEL_CLANG_COMPILER so that we can take a path through the Intel header files
6388  // that avoids editing header Intel specific header files to handle builtin functions that
6389  // use types defined in the header files.
6390  inputCommandLine.push_back("-D__INTEL_CLANG_COMPILER");
6391 #endif
6392  }
6393  j++;
6394  }
